datasets.title: Palestine - Geodata of Damage Assessment in Beit Hanun, Gaza Strip - Occupied Palestinian Territory
datasets.description: This map illustrates satellite-detected damage and destruction in the Beit Hanun area, Gaza Strip, resulting from ongoing violence in the area. Using a satellite image collected 25 July 2014 by the Pleiades satellite, and compared with a pre-crisis Pleiades image collected 6 July 2014, UNOSAT analysis has identified 214 destroyed structures, 122 severely damaged structures, and 103 moderately damaged structures. In addition, 32 craters on roads and in agricultural and non-urbanized areas are also visible as of 25 July 2014. Note that a certain portion of the image analyzed by UNOSAT was downsampled, so the confidence level for the analysis in this area is 'uncertain' (103 structures). This is a preliminary analysis and has not yet been validated in the field. Please send ground feedback to UNITAR/UNOSAT.. [Source: This metadata record was automatically extracted from the Humanitarian Data Exchange (HDX); Original dataset: https://data.humdata.org/dataset/geodata-of-damage-assessment-in-beit-hanun-gaza-strip-occupied-palestinian-te-july-28-2014]
datasets.details: This is a preliminary assessment and has not yet been validated in the field. It is important to consider the characteristics of the source imagery used in the analyses when interpreting results. For damage assessments it should be noted that only significant damage to the structural integrity of the buildings analyzed can be seen in imagery, while minor damage such as cracks or holes may not be visible at all. For flood extractions using radar data it is important to note that urban areas and highly vegetated areas may mask the flood signature and result in underestimation of flood waters. Users with specific questions or concerns should contact unosat@unitar.org to seek clarification.

lineage.description: UNOSAT analysts compared Pleiades satellite imagery from 6 July 2014 (pre-crisis) and 25 July 2014 (post-crisis) over Beit Hanun, Gaza Strip, using visual interpretation to identify and classify damaged structures (destroyed, severely damaged, moderately damaged) and infrastructure impacts (craters). Results were vectorized as point and polygon features with damage classification attributes.
